ADR-0028 tradeoff ACCEPTED (2026-07-01, ground-truthed via retest FIXED=False). Turn-1 Active Cinderace (160hp, 1W), bench 2x Staryu, Hero's Cape (+100 ACE SPEC) in hand, opp Cinderace can afford Turbo Flare (50). Human wanted End (hold the Cape for the main attacker). Branch(3) of _tool_deploy_slot deploys it on Cinderace: opp incoming 50, _survival_gain(160,50,100)=2>=1, so the wall 'gains a turn'; branch(1) can't pick a benched Staryu (0 incoming) and branch(2) skips (Cinderace not the wincon). We ACCEPT branch(3)'s proactive survival-turns deploy over holding — the deck runs 6 hand-shuffle Supporters that would otherwise bury the one-of ACE SPEC, so parking it on the surviving body beats a bare hold. Known accepted limitation: Cinderace is a terminal Stage-2 (<-Raboot) so the Cape can't ride up to Mega Starmie ex; branch(3) treats the ACE SPEC like a fungible +HP tool. Kept as-is by design decision, not fixed.

ADR-0028 tradeoff ACCEPTED (2026-07-01, retested through the real Pilot): the original shuffle-away blunder IS gone — the Pilot no longer plays Lillie's; it deploys the Cape. But branch(3) of _tool_deploy_slot (survival-turns wall) targets the Active Cinderace (130hp, gains a turn vs incoming) over the human's benched Staryu, because the benched wincon-line Staryu takes 0 incoming so branch(1) can't select it. We accept branch(3)'s present-survival targeting over save-for-the-wincon-line: the exact body (Cinderace vs Staryu) is overruled by the doctrine. NB the anti-shuffle argument does NOT favour Cinderace over Staryu here (both are shuffle-safe) — this is purely present-survival > future-wincon value; the residual suboptimality (ACE SPEC on a non-transferable off-line wall) is a known, accepted limitation of branch(3).
